title: What is Life All About?
description: In this program Dr. Rashad Khalifa argues that the world's biggest problem is neither war, disease nor poverty but that people do not know who they are, mistaking the body they see in a mirror for the self. He distinguishes body from soul, calls the body a garment worn for fifty or a hundred years, and observes that people feed the body three meals a day while giving the real person nothing, describing the soul as literally a piece of the breath God breathed into Adam and claiming it can grow to immense size when nourished. He says the nourishment is a specific method rather than vague spirituality or ordinary supplication: five daily contacts with God following what he compares to the numerical combination of a safe, with fasting as a further practice, and he offers newly obtained mathematically coded evidence as his authority. Citing the Barbara Hutton story and Eddie Murphy's interview with Barbara Walters as cases of wealth without happiness, he closes by inviting viewers to examine the physical evidence free of charge, giving an address on East 6th Street in Tucson and a telephone number.

title: Who is GOD?
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa argues that idol worship persists because people do not grasp the greatness of God, and devotes the sermon to establishing that scale from what he presents as established scientific facts. He works outward from the solar system, whose sunlight reaches Earth in four minutes and whose span runs to billions of miles, to the Milky Way, which light would take a hundred thousand years to cross, to a neighboring galaxy two million light years away, to a universe of a billion galaxies and a billion trillion stars measuring some 26 billion light years across, pausing to calculate that merely counting a quintillion stars at one per second would take 32 billion years. He then states, on the authority of the Quran and its mathematical code, that this universe is the smallest and innermost of seven, so that no number can express the circumference of the outermost, and cites Sura 39:67 on the heavens held in God's hand as an allegory for that greatness. He concludes that against this scale it is blasphemous to attribute to God a son, wife or mother, or to idolize Muhammad, Jesus, Mary or a saint, asking what role any of them played in setting the synchronized rotation of the moon or the precision of the orbits. Related recording: this carries the same audio as "38 - Friday Sermon Who is GOD Understanding Our Universe (08-04-1988)" in this collection. description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa teaches a beginner's course in reading and writing Arabic, starting from the assumption that the viewer knows nothing of the language. title: Debate: Dr Rashad Khalifa Ph D vs Sunni Scholars (1987)

description: A 1987 debate in Arabic, presented here in English translation, between Dr. Rashad Khalifa and a group of Sunni scholars. Both sides agree at the outset that every messenger called to the worship of God alone, but divide over the means: the scholars hold that the Quran states some matters in general terms and that the messenger's Sunna supplies the detail, citing Sura 16:44 on proclaiming to the people, Sura 59:7 and Sura 4:80 on obeying the messenger, and hadiths about being given "the Quran and something like it alongside it." Khalifa answers from Sura 6:114 and Sura 7:52 that the Quran is fully detailed, that Sura 5:99 limits the messenger's role to delivery, and that the number of prayer units and the rites of hajj and zakat reached Muhammad already established through the religion of Abraham, offering an analogy about a product already on the market and attributing his own knowledge of them to mass transmission and to the universal agreement of Muslims. The exchange, pressed hard from both sides and briefly interrupted by a dispute over a camera at the window, moves to the shahada, with Khalifa arguing from Sura 3:18, Sura 2:285 and Sura 72:18 that adding Muhammad's name beside God's in the testimony and the call to prayer is an innovation and a distinction among messengers, while the scholars insist the testimony is Quranic and press him on whether he denies that Muhammad is the messenger of God.
